verdict: CEILING CARTOGRAPHY (ceiling_cartography.py): training-free test of whether ANY door past the ~0.62 retrieval oracle is open, to decide if v7 should be a model at all. 3 splits, held-out K562. DOOR 1 REACHABILITY: a KO's input features reach 86% of the train-restricted true-profile oracle (0.512 vs 0.597); current v5 (~0.5) sits +0.012 from that input-reachable ceiling. DOOR 2 GENERATION: an NMF program basis reconstructing the TRUE held-out profile recalls 0.679 (best r=256) vs oracle ~0.62; loading-shuffle 0.130; and inputs predict the loadings at 0.246 vs 0.211 mean-baseline -> OPEN-IN-PRINCIPLE-SHUT-IN-PRACTICE (generation ceiling 0.679 > 0.62 and KO-specific, but the true loadings predict from inputs at only 0.246 -- below v5 ~0.50 -- so a decoder would score WORSE than current retrieval; not worth building unless the loadings become far more predictable). DOOR 3 CROSS-LINE: transferring the same KO's other-line |z| to K562 recalls 0.183 vs the same-subset K562 oracle 0.607 (wrong-KO 0.034, marginal 0.250) -> SHUT (the K562-specific residue does not transfer across lines). ALL THREE DOORS SHUT: 0.62 is confirmed a DATA ceiling (the K562-specific residue is idiosyncratic, unreachable from inputs, not low-rank-compositional, and non-transferring across lines). v7 should NOT be a heavier retrieval/generation model -- the honest v7 is a calibrated selective-prediction wrapper on v5 that reports which predictions to trust. Deterministic; no training.
